title: Greedy Best-First on New York (SoHo) ⚡
description: Visualizing Greedy Best-First pathfinding on New York (SoHo)
ig_caption:
Greedy Best-First Search vs A*: Pathfinding Comparison — Why it rushes to the destination ⚡ (and when it fails)

In this Barcelona (Eixample) grid, Greedy Best-First expands the node with the lowest heuristic h(n), like “distance to the goal,” without caring how you got there.

✅ Greedy Best-First (GBFS):
- Priority = h(n) only
- Can look brilliant in open areas
- Ignores g(n) (path cost so far)

❌ When it fails:
- If your heuristic “lies” about the true route, GBFS can chase a near-goal corridor that dead-ends or loops
- It may explore fewer “wrong turns” early—but keep committing to them

🆚 Greedy vs A*:
- A* uses f(n)=g(n)+h(n), balancing “where you are” + “where you’re going”
- GBFS is faster to react, but more fragile when obstacles create misleading shortcuts

Takeaway: If your heuristic is optimistic AND consistent with the map’s geometry, Greedy Best-First can fly. If not, A*’s cost-awareness is your safety net.

Debate: Should we prioritize “distance-to-go” for speed, or “total cost” for reliability? 👇
